scope: Ninth expansion batch: 12 exercises, three each for kagiri evidence scope, baai procedural case framing, an affirmative condition maintained with kagiri, and a negative necessary condition with nai kagiri. These are selected core functions, not every lexical, suffix or emphatic use of kagiri.

sources.section: Kagiri explanation: limits on the scope of a statement, information or perception as the scope of a claim, and conditions under which a result holds; standard verb forms and noun + de aru attachment. The source's broad limiting analysis does not make these functions interchangeable in every sentence.
Inspected the negative-condition example 明日は、雨が降らない限り、10時に学校で会いましょう. Used for the nai-form conditional, not as a claim that every negative kagiri clause has a negative main clause.
Baai wa: a case or situation; attachment with no after nouns and na after na-adjectives. The source's categorical claim excluding all controlled or planned events is not adopted.

authoringNotes: All scenarios are newly authored. Source explanations support the core constructions; exact sentences, answer spellings and distractor rationales require independent linguistic review.

The seven noun-choice questions visibly restrict the list to kagiri and baai and state the intended frame. The necessary-registration and continuing-study items form a reciprocal maintained-condition-versus-case relationship, separate from evidence-scope-versus-case. Do not misattribute that continuing-condition distractor to the evidential construction.

The other five questions visibly request dictionary or nai forms of the supplied verb before printed kagiri. Kana and standard kanji spellings are accepted; other natural temporal or conditional formulations fall outside the stated literal-blank task.

Each negative-necessary-condition example supplies an additional requirement. This makes the necessary-versus-sufficient distinction concrete rather than letting a learner infer guaranteed admission, borrowing or acceptance from the prerequisite alone.
Evidence-scope items use knowledge, a completed investigation and direct visual inspection, each with an explicit limit. Baai items cover noun + no, a past verb and a na-adjective + na.

Screen the full article inventory: toki, uchi, aida and baai may overlap with conditional kagiri; tame may introduce a cause; expressions with hodo/dake can concern extent without replacing each kagiri construction. Do not label all such alternatives ungrammatical outside the controlled task.

All prior 119 exercise records remain unchanged. One SRS identity per exercise, not per spelling or choose/type presentation. This batch does not claim unrestricted discrimination between all conditional and temporal expressions.
